classification.difficultyReason: Infer exact radian endpoints from standard cosine, sine and tangent features, excluding a tangent asymptote.

content.prompt: The following show the standard trigonometric graphs, but with restricted domains. Find the domain.

spec.description: Restricted cosine graph starting at its maximum on the y-axis and ending at its next rising zero after the minimum. Arrowed axes, y ticks at 1 and −1, no numerical x labels, grid, shading or endpoint markers.
spec.answerVisibility: The curve and y labels are permanent givens; the domain and numerical x coordinates are omitted from the student graph.

answer.worked:
The cosine graph starts at its maximum when $x=0$. After the minimum at $x=\pi$, it ends at the rising zero where $x=\frac{3\pi}{2}$. Both endpoints are included.

$$D=\left[0,\frac{3\pi}{2}\right].$$

spec.description: Restricted sine graph starting at the origin, passing through a maximum and minimum, and ending at its second positive maximum. Arrowed axes, y ticks at 1 and −1, no numerical x labels, grid, shading or endpoint markers.
spec.answerVisibility: The curve and y labels are permanent givens; the domain and numerical x coordinates are omitted from the student graph.

answer.worked:
The sine graph starts at the origin and completes one cycle at $x=2\pi$. It continues to the next maximum at $x=\frac{5\pi}{2}$. Both endpoints are included.

$$D=\left[0,\frac{5\pi}{2}\right].$$

spec.description: Two increasing tangent branches separated by a dashed vertical asymptote left of the y-axis. The left branch begins at an x-axis intercept and has an upward arrow. The right branch has a downward arrow, passes through the origin and ends at a black filled point with a horizontal dashed guide to y=1. No numerical x labels, grid or shading.
spec.mathematics: y = tan x on [−π,−π/2) ∪ (−π/2,π/4], with vertical asymptote x=−π/2 and closed endpoint (π/4,1). Finite plotting bounds show the unbounded branches using arrows.
spec.answerVisibility: The curve, asymptote, branch arrows, y=1 guide and closed endpoint are permanent givens; domain endpoints and the asymptote's x coordinate are omitted from the student graph.

inlines.text: Exclude the vertical asymptote; include both finite endpoints.

answer.worked:
The left intercept is at $x=-\pi$. The right endpoint has $y=1$, so its coordinate is $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$. Both finite endpoints are included. Tangent is undefined at the dashed vertical asymptote $x=-\frac{\pi}{2}$, which must be excluded.

$$D=\left[-\pi,-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\cup\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{4}\right].$$
